subject: Re: Private/VPC deployment — Post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Tom Baker <tbaker@globalmed.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Khan <a.khan@globalmed.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment discovery follow-up

Marissa — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side so we have the same understanding and can get the infra team looped in:

- Drivers: regulatory requirement for data residency (PHI) and an internal policy preferring air-gapped or VPC-based on-prem deployments for inference.
- Networking constraints: GlobalMed will not allow outbound internet egress from model hosts except through an approved proxy; preferred connectivity is via Direct Connect / Private Peering or an on-prem air-gapped option.
- Security: strong interest in KMS integration (customer-managed keys), SOC 2 evidence, audit logs for prompt/response access, and RBAC for model access.
- Ops goals: predictable latency (95th < 300ms for QA flows), capacity for peak inference during business hours, and clear playbook for upgrades/rollbacks.

Open questions we flagged on the call: expected queries per month (tokens), preferred model family, whether there is a preference for GPU type (A100 vs H100), and storage/network limits for caching model artifacts.

Next steps from GlobalMed: I will share our firewall rules and the primary network contact (IT infra). From Redwood — a short architecture doc, network checklist, and an itemized list of info you need from our side. Can you confirm timeline for a technical deep-dive with our infra team? We are available next week Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Tom Baker
Director, AI Systems
GlobalMed

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private deployment discovery follow-up — Redwood recap & next steps

Tom — really appreciate the clear summary. Recap from our side + concrete next steps below. I copied Dev and Monica to help with technical and sizing details.

Summary of what we heard:
- Regulatory: PHI/data residency -> Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) required.
- Network: no general outbound egress; need private peering or air-gap.
- Security: customer-managed KMS, audit logs, RBAC, SOC 2 evidence required.
- SLOs: target 95th latency < 300ms for QA flows; we also discussed a 10–20ms variability budget for within-region requests.

What Redwood will provide (attachments included):
- redwood-private-vpc-architecture.pdf: high-level architecture options (VPC peering, private peering, on-prem air-gapped appliance).
- network-checklist.xlsx: checklist your network team can use (ports, IP ranges, proxy config, firewall rules we need to whitelist).

Action items / next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with GlobalMed infra + Redwood infra team (Dev) — propose Wed 2026-09-09 09:30 PT. Please confirm.
2) Dev will send a short questionnaire on throughput and model usage (tokens/month, concurrency, max sequence length).
3) We will prepare an initial sizing and a draft statement of work for Private deployment options (VPC vs air-gap).
4) Procurement: if you can share the procurement contact, we’ll include a timeline and pricing scenarios (dedicated reserved capacity vs on-prem license).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and share a short pre-call form for your infra team to fill out.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0147

Subject: Follow-up — technical specifics we need before deep-dive

Tom / Marissa — quick technical note ahead of the infra call so we can hit the ground running. Could you confirm the following items (short bullets are fine):
- Expected tokens/month (or requests/day) and peak concurrency at any given second.
- Typical request size and max sequence length (prompt + expected completion).
- Whether the model will be a fine-tuned private variant or a standard open checkpoint.
- Whether GlobalMed requires full air-gap (no network at all) or private peering with limited egress through a proxy.
- Preferred GPU family (if any) or whether we should recommend a cost/latency-balanced profile.

Also, for private deployments we’ll want to understand your uptime SLO target and whether you need on-call escalation via Redwood.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Marissa / Dev — thanks, that all looks good. Confirming:
- We can do the deep-dive Wed 2026-09-09 09:30 PT.
- Quick answers to your questions: tokens/month ~ 150M; peak concurrency ~ 60 requests/sec; typical prompt+response ~ 1.2k tokens; target 95th latency < 300ms.
- We prefer private peering (Direct Connect) over a fully air-gapped install but need the option for an on-prem appliance if SOC/clinical audits require it.
- We do want customer-managed KMS and full audit logging.

Procurement contact: Aisha Khan (a.khan@globalmed.com) — she’ll loop in our SOW/procurement team after the tech call.

Attached firewall rules (sent earlier) and I’ve copied IT to ensure we can exchange the additional checklist.

See you on the 9th — Tom
